area: remaining focus geometry and Lie groups

reviews.evidence: The source defines the category with smooth manifolds as objects and smooth maps as morphisms; the listed category, manifold, and map prerequisites are used in the definition.
The source defines the group of diffeomorphisms under composition and inversion; diffeomorphism and smooth-manifold foundations are direct, while the category page supplies the ambient category.
The source defines an embedded submanifold through a smooth embedding and its induced subspace smooth structure; manifold, chart, subspace topology, and embedding are direct.
The source constructs the product smooth structure from two smooth manifolds and the product topology; those are precisely the direct inputs.
The source defines tangent vectors as derivations/equivalence classes at a point of a smooth manifold and equips them with vector-space operations; manifold and vector-space foundations are direct.
The source defines curvature by dω plus one-half of the Lie bracket wedge term for a principal connection; connection form, exterior derivative, Lie bracket, and principal connection are direct.
The source defines a diffeomorphism as a bijective smooth map with smooth inverse; smooth map/manifold and bijection/inverse-function prerequisites are direct.
The source defines the differential of a smooth map as the induced linear map between tangent spaces; smooth maps, tangent spaces, and linear maps are direct.
The source forms the exterior power fiberwise from a vector bundle and its transition maps; vector bundle, tensor product, and bundle morphism inputs are direct.
The source defines a fibered manifold as a smooth map that is a surjective submersion; smooth manifold/map, submersion, and surjectivity are direct.
The source proves the Maurer–Cartan equation for the left Maurer–Cartan form using Lie-group multiplication, exterior differentiation, and the Lie bracket; all listed inputs are used.
The source defines a Lie bracket as a bilinear alternating operation on a vector space; vector-space and linear-map prerequisites are direct.
The source defines a Lie group as a smooth manifold with smooth group operations; group, smooth manifold, and smooth map foundations are direct.
The source defines a horizontal distribution/connection on a principal bundle invariant under the Lie-group action; principal bundle and Lie group are direct.
The source states the connection-form reproduction property on fundamental vector fields; vector-field structure is the direct prerequisite.
The source defines a smooth right action of a Lie group on a smooth manifold; Lie group, manifold, and action data are direct.
The source defines a section as a smooth right inverse of a smooth fiber-bundle projection; the bundle and smooth-map prerequisites are direct.
The source defines an embedding as an injective immersion that is a homeomorphism onto its image; smooth map/manifold, immersion, injectivity, topology, and image are direct.
The source defines an immersion by injectivity of the differential on tangent spaces; smooth maps, tangent spaces, differential, and injectivity are direct.
The source defines a submersion by surjectivity of the differential; smooth maps, tangent spaces, differential, and surjectivity are direct.
The source constructs the tangent space at a point from smooth curves/derivations and gives it a vector-space structure; manifold and linear algebra prerequisites are direct.
The source defines tensor products fiberwise and assembles them into a bundle; smooth manifold is the only base prerequisite listed and is used in the construction.
The source defines a vector field as a smooth section of the tangent bundle; manifold, tangent bundle, section, and tangent-space foundations are direct.
The source defines a vector subbundle by locally constant-rank linear subspaces with smooth local trivializations; vector bundle, subspace, trivialization, and embedding are direct.
The source defines the vertical tangent space as the kernel of the differential of a fiber projection; fibered manifold, bundle map, tangent bundle, and embedded fiber are direct.
The source defines the wedge product by antisymmetrizing tensor products of differential forms; smooth manifold, forms, and tangent spaces are direct.
The source defines a Lie algebra as a vector space with an alternating bilinear bracket satisfying Jacobi; vector-space and bracket prerequisites are direct.
The source constructs the Lie algebra as the tangent space at the identity with bracket from invariant vector fields; tangent-space and Lie-group prerequisites are direct.
